bites.title: Three kinds of profit
bites.html:
Accounting profit = TR − explicit costs (money really paid out).

Economic profit = accounting profit − implicit costs (what the owner gives up: a salary elsewhere, rent for their own equipment).

Normal profit = economic profit of 0.

bites.title: Try it with numbers
bites.html: Solve it step by step. Press New numbers and do it again until it feels easy.

bites.q: TR = 1,200, explicit costs = 700, the owner could earn 200 elsewhere and rent out equipment for 150. Economic profit?
bites.why: Accounting profit = 1,200 − 700 = 500. Implicit costs = 200 + 150 = 350. Economic profit = 500 − 350 = 150.

bites.title: The golden rule: MR = MC
bites.html:
Look only at the next piece:

  • MC > MR → it costs more than it brings → produce less
  • MC < MR → it brings more than it costs → produce more
  • MR = MC → the optimum

This rule works in every market structure.

bites.title: Price-taker: d = AR = MR = P
bites.html:
In perfect competition many small firms sell an identical product, so no firm can change the price. The firm's demand is a horizontal line at the market price: every extra piece brings exactly P.

So the golden rule MR = MC becomes P = MC.

bites.q: What does the demand curve facing ONE perfectly competitive firm look like?
bites.why: The firm can sell any quantity at the market price: d = AR = MR = P. Only the market demand slopes down.

bites.title: See it: move the price
bites.html: Move the price. Green rectangle = profit, red = loss. Watch what happens below 15 (min AVC).

bites.title: Decisions of a perfectly competitive firm

steps.html: AVC = 16 + Q = 43. P = 70 > AVC, and the loss 71 < FC 800, so keep producing in the short run.

bites.q: P is above AVC but below AC. In the short run the firm should…
options: keep producing, its loss is smaller than FC
shut down, it makes a loss
bites.why: Revenue covers all variable costs and part of FC. Shutting down would make the loss equal to the whole FC.

options: Shut-down: P = min AVC · Break-even: P = min AC
Shut-down: P = min AC · Break-even: P = min AVC
Shut-down: TR = TC · Break-even: TR = VC
bites.why: Shut-down: TR = VC, loss = FC (short run). Break-even: TR = TC, economic profit 0 (long run).

units.title: Topics 7–8 · Equilibrium, surplus and imperfect competition

bites.title: Equilibrium: Qd = Qs
bites.html:
Above the equilibrium price → surplus → the price falls. Below it → shortage → the price rises.

Perfect competition is allocatively efficient: MU = MC.

bites.title: Consumer and producer surplus
bites.html:
CS = TU − real expenditure (under demand, above the price).
PS = Σ(P − MC) = TR − VC (above supply, under the price).

bites.q: Supply and demand both rise, supply rises more. The price…
options: we can't say anything about Q either
bites.why: ΔS > ΔD → P falls. The quantity rises.

bites.title: Ceiling and floor
bites.html:
Ceiling (max price) below P* → shortage, e.g. regulated rents.
Floor (min price) above P* → surplus, e.g. subsidised farm prices.

bites.title: Imperfect competition
bites.html:
At least one seller can affect the price → the firm's demand slopes down → MR < P.

Same rule: MR = MC gives Q. Then go up to demand for the price. P > MC → deadweight loss.
